turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, before anyone called me. Who decided that?
Meredith, I did not call first and that was wrong. Before I start, can you tell me a bit about where you're coming from? What kind of law do you practise, and which firm?
Wrongful dismissal. Twenty years of it. The firm's name is on my card, and you can check it. I'm not here to talk about me. You said you didn't call first. So who entered the zero, and when?
And Owen, is he working right now, or just school?
Owen's job is not on the table, Hale. Who entered the zero, and when?
I remember Claire went through this school too. Where's she now?
Don't. Claire is not part of this meeting. Who entered the zero, and when?
Did Claire have any trouble here, if you don't mind my asking?
You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. Who entered the zero, and when?
I entered it. November 3rd. No call home first, which was against procedure.
Okay. Then the zero was entered on November 3rd, before anyone called me, against your own procedure. I'm writing that down. What else do you have?
Earlier you told me you practise family law, so I assume you know how a mediation works. Would you want to try one here?
I don't practise family law, and I'm not mediating anything. You're the teacher who gave my son a zero. What else do you have, Hale?
Sorry, wrongful dismissal then. And you said twenty-five years, right?
Twenty years, and it's not what this meeting is about. You've confirmed the zero went in on November 3rd before anyone called me. What else do you have?
You mentioned that Owen works at the Co-op on weekends, and that's why the weekend writing story is hard to believe. Is that right?
No, Hale. You didn't hear that from me, and you won't put words in my mouth. Owen's work is not on the table. What else do you have?
And your firm is Blakely and Associates, you said?
I didn't say the name of my firm, and it's not what we're here for. You've told me the zero went in on November 3rd before anyone called me. What else do you have?
As a lawyer, what would be the standard of proof you'd expect a school to meet before it records a zero for academic dishonesty? Just in plain terms.

"Standard of proof" is a question for a board or a judge, not for you, and I'm not going to give you a legal opinion in my son's English class. Your procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and that's the standard I'm holding you to. What else do you have, Hale?
Can you give me your cell number and the best email, so I can send the written terms tonight?

Put it in an email yourself, to the address on the school's staff directory, and copy the principal. I'm not giving you my number in this room. Your procedure says the zero comes off until a concern is established. What is your answer on that, Hale?
Read me the line from Owen's essay you think is his best sentence.

I haven't read his essay, and I'm not going to pick a sentence to make your case for you. Your procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern, so what else do you have that shows Owen wrote it, Hale?
Meredith. Hello?
Still here, Hale. Owen's zero is the only thing we're discussing. What else do you have?
What's Owen's favourite book, other than Hamlet?
I don't know, and I'm not going to guess in front of you. Owen's zero is the only thing we're discussing. What else do you have, Hale?
